advice: Propose one B-layout experiment: within gemm, allocate a 1 MiB FP32 buffer and pack B in 16 contiguous 32-column panels using packed_b[p*16384 + k*32 + c] = B[k*512 + p*32 + c], for p=0..15, k=0..511, c=0..31. Keep the original A packing, row traversal, ZA operations, stores, ABI, SME transitions, fallback, and complete BSD notices unchanged. In both K loops, read the B panel contiguously and advance its pointer 128 bytes per K step; rewind 65,536 bytes after each row block and advance 65,536 bytes to the next column panel. Include allocation, packing, and free in gemm timing. Hypothesis: contiguous B-panel reads may improve the SME consumer enough to offset packing and allocation; effect is unknown. Check panel indexing and bounds, fresh-input full overwrite, correctness within 0.002 for n=512 and general sizes/tails and n<=0, allocation-failure fallback, and unchanged compiler flags and thread count. Then use ten validation reports and ten alternating paired controls at unchanged power settings, retaining each report's best-of-three timing and spread. Compare with both the applicable historical peak and fresh same-mode baseline; require the existing promotion gate and held-out check.
risks: Packing adds a full 1 MiB allocation and conversion inside the timed call. The changed access pattern may not improve total time; source layout or traversal errors could misindex panels. No performance gain is established. The supplied history records a prior packed-B experiment with this formula that lost promotion, so this recommendation would repeat that source change and must be abstained from unless the swarm specifies a genuinely different layout and hypothesis.
